questions.stem: One who has no faith in the existence of God.
questions.explanation: B is correct. An atheist denies the existence of God. An agnostic believes it is unknowable; a theist believes in God.

questions.stem: A person who travels to a holy place as an act of devotion.
questions.explanation: C is correct. A pilgrim travels to a sacred place for religious reasons. A nomad/vagrant moves without a fixed destination.

questions.stem: A speech delivered without any prior preparation.
questions.explanation: C is correct. Extempore (or impromptu) means delivered without preparation. A soliloquy is a character's thoughts spoken aloud; a monologue is a long solo speech.

questions.stem: One who eats both plants and animals.
questions.explanation: C is correct. Omnivore (Latin: omni = all). Herbivore = plants only; Carnivore = flesh only; Insectivore = insects.

questions.stem: A place where bees are kept.
questions.explanation: B is correct. Apiary (Latin: apis = bee). Aviary = birds; Aquarium = fish; Sanatorium = recovering patients.

questions.stem: The scientific study of coins and medals.
questions.explanation: B is correct. Numismatics = study of coins. Philately = stamp collecting; Heraldry = coats of arms; Genealogy = family history.

questions.stem: One who believes in or practises self-discipline and abstains from pleasure.
questions.explanation: B is correct. An ascetic deliberately avoids sensual pleasures. A stoic endures pain without complaint; a hedonist pursues pleasure; a cynic distrusts human sincerity.

questions.stem: A doctor who specialises in the diagnosis and treatment of mental disorders.
questions.explanation: C is correct. A psychiatrist is a medical doctor who treats mental illness. A psychologist studies behaviour but is not a medical doctor; a neurologist treats brain/nerve disorders.

questions.stem: Government by the mob or the undisciplined masses.
questions.explanation: C is correct. Mobocracy = rule by a mob. Theocracy = rule by clergy; Oligarchy = rule by a few; Plutocracy = rule by the wealthy.

questions.stem: An extreme or irrational fear of being in enclosed spaces.
questions.explanation: B is correct. Claustrophobia = fear of confined spaces (Latin: claustrum = enclosed). Agoraphobia = fear of open/public places; Xenophobia = fear of foreigners; Hydrophobia = fear of water.
